\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نتج} (nataja)}{نتج (nataja)}]{\ar{نتج} (nataja) — to stem from; to result}

\label{lesson:AR-C414-nataja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to recur, then the Arabic for to endure.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نتج}}
\textbf{\ar{نتج}} — \emph{nataja} — \textquotedblleft{}to stem from; to result\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نتج} \ar{الحريق} \ar{عن} \ar{خطأ} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nataja al-ḥarīq ʿan khaṭaʾ ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fire resulted from a small mistake.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتج}, \emph{yantij}.

It takes \ar{عن}: \ar{نتج} \ar{عن} …. The noun \ar{نتيجة} is a result.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نتج}} (\emph{nataja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-t-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to bring forth young\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Nataja} is a Form I verb: to come forth from a thing, to result.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nataja}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nataja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nataja al-ḥarīq ʿan khaṭaʾ ṣaghīr.} — The fire resulted from a small mistake.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to recur, then the Arabic for to endure, then say \emph{nataja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نتج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To stem from; to result\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ترتب} (tarattaba)}{ترتب (tarattaba)}]{\ar{ترتب} (tarattaba) — to follow from}

\label{lesson:AR-C414-tarattaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to endure, then the Arabic for to stem from.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ترتب}}
\textbf{\ar{ترتب}} — \emph{tarattaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to follow from\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ترتب} \ar{على} \ar{القرار} \ar{تغييرات} \ar{كثيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tarattaba ʿalā al-qarār taghyīrāt kathīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many changes followed from the decision.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يترتب}, \emph{yatarattab}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{ترتب} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ترتب}} (\emph{tarattaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-t-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be firm, fixed in place\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to fall into rank after a thing: to follow from it. \ar{رتب}, to tidy, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarattaba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarattaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarattaba ʿalā al-qarār taghyīrāt kathīra.} — Many changes followed from the decision.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to endure, then the Arabic for to stem from, then say \emph{tarattaba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ترتب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To follow from\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انعكس} (inʿakasa)}{انعكس (inʿakasa)}]{\ar{انعكس} (inʿakasa) — to be reflected}

\label{lesson:AR-C414-inakasa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to stem from, then the Arabic for to follow from.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انعكس}}
\textbf{\ar{انعكس}} — \emph{inʿakasa} — \textquotedblleft{}to be reflected\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انعكس} \ar{التوتر} \ar{على} \ar{صحته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inʿakasa at-tawattur ʿalā ṣiḥḥatih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The stress was reflected in his health.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينعكس}, \emph{yanʿakis}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{انعكس} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انعكس}} (\emph{inʿakasa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-k-s}, \textquotedblleft{}to reverse, to turn back\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII, to be turned back: to be reflected, like light from a mirror.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿakasa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿakasa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inʿakasa at-tawattur ʿalā ṣiḥḥatih.} — The stress was reflected in his health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to stem from, then the Arabic for to follow from, then say \emph{inʿakasa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انعكس} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To be reflected\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عاقبة} (ʿāqiba)}{عاقبة (ʿāqiba)}]{\ar{عاقبة} (ʿāqiba) — a consequence}

\label{lesson:AR-C414-aqiba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to follow from, then the Arabic for to be reflected.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عاقبة}}
\textbf{\ar{عاقبة}} — \emph{ʿāqiba} — \textquotedblleft{}a consequence\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لم} \ar{يفكر} \ar{الرجل} \ar{في} \ar{العاقبة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lam yufakkir ar-rajul fī al-ʿāqiba.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The man did not think about the consequence.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{عواقب}, \emph{ʿawāqib}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عاقبة}} (\emph{ʿāqiba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-q-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to come after, to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lane). An \emph{ʿāqiba} is what comes after a thing: its end, its consequence.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāqiba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿāqiba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lam yufakkir ar-rajul fī al-ʿāqiba.} — The man did not think about the consequence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to follow from, then the Arabic for to be reflected, then say \emph{ʿāqiba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عاقبة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A consequence\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأثير} (taʾthīr)}{تأثير (taʾthīr)}]{\ar{تأثير} (taʾthīr) — an effect}

\label{lesson:AR-C414-tathir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to be reflected, then the Arabic for a consequence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأثير}}
\textbf{\ar{تأثير}} — \emph{taʾthīr} — \textquotedblleft{}an effect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{للنوم} \ar{تأثير} \ar{كبير} \ar{على} \ar{الصحة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{li-n-nawm taʾthīr kabīr ʿalā aṣ-ṣiḥḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sleep has a big effect on health.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأثير}} (\emph{taʾthīr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-th-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a trace, a track\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Taʾthīr} is the Form II verbal noun, leaving a trace on something: an effect, an influence.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾthīr}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾthīr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-n-nawm taʾthīr kabīr ʿalā aṣ-ṣiḥḥa.} — Sleep has a big effect on health.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to be reflected, then the Arabic for a consequence, then say \emph{taʾthīr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تأثير} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An effect\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
